name: terminalDemo
description: Visible AND captured. For each curl: open a real Terminal.app window on the macOS agent 'ashu-mac' (via osascript) that runs the curl, tee's its output to a temp file, and drops a .done marker (so you watch it run on-screen); wait 5 seconds; then a headless cap.shell_exec waits for the .done marker and reads the temp file back so the response is also returned to the server. Two paced steps run in sequence: terminal A (httpbin.org/get), then terminal B (httpbin.org/uuid).
rationale: Demo variant combining the visible Terminal.app approach (osascript do script) with server-side capture (tee to a temp file + read it back). The osascript do script returns immediately while the curl runs asynchronously inside Terminal, so a fixed wait can read the file before the curl finishes (observed: a 5s wait returned an empty capture). The read node therefore polls for a .done marker (up to ~40s) before cat-ing the file, while the 5s control.wait is kept purely for visible pacing. control.wait runs on the server; the osascript and read nodes run on ashu-mac. cap.shell_exec must be granted to the tenant.

argv: tell application "Terminal" to do script "rm -f /tmp/aakaar_demo_a.done; curl -sS --max-time 30 https://httpbin.org/get | tee /tmp/aakaar_demo_a.txt; touch /tmp/aakaar_demo_a.done"
for i in $(seq 1 40); do [ -f /tmp/aakaar_demo_a.done ] && break; sleep 1; done; cat /tmp/aakaar_demo_a.txt
tell application "Terminal" to do script "rm -f /tmp/aakaar_demo_b.done; curl -sS --max-time 30 https://httpbin.org/uuid | tee /tmp/aakaar_demo_b.txt; touch /tmp/aakaar_demo_b.done"
for i in $(seq 1 40); do [ -f /tmp/aakaar_demo_b.done ] && break; sleep 1; done; cat /tmp/aakaar_demo_b.txt
